headline: Software development, grounded in real workflows.
introduction: I'm an NBCC Software Development student building Android apps in Kotlin, Windows applications in C#, and a Python learning simulator. My work connects real-world requirements with application architecture, automated testing, and useful workflows.
about: I am completing the Information Technology: Software Development program at New Brunswick Community College, with expected graduation in 2027. My personal projects span Android with Kotlin, Windows desktop software with C# and WPF, and a Python learning simulator. In class, I am building a broader foundation in web development, database programming, and software design.

I bring a customer-service and operations mindset to software: clarify what should happen, document blockers and edge cases, and verify changes across the paths people use. I am interested in work that connects implementation, product thinking, and careful quality checks.

I am pursuing software development opportunities where I can build useful applications, learn from an experienced team, and work closely with the people using the software. Longer term, I plan to continue university study and explore research where developmental biology, computer science, and cognitive science meet. My current bioelectric simulator is a learning project that reflects that curiosity.
